courses.title: General Chemistry I
courses.description: [GE 5A] Fundamental principles and concepts of chemistry, including atomic and molecular structure; nomenclature; stoichiometry; solution chemistry, including acid-base and redox chemistry; quantum theory; periodic properties; bonding theory; thermochemistry; gases; and intermolecular forces. Corequisite(s): CHM 1210L .
courses.prerequisites: SAT Math>=550; ACT Math>=23; ALEKS >=76; C or better in MAT 12, 105, 106, 112, 114, 115, 116, 120, 125, 130, 191, 214, 216, 224, MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , MAT 1060 , MAT 1070 , MAT 1140 , MAT 1150 , MAT 1200 , MAT 1250 , MAT 1300 , MAT 1310 , MAT 1910 , MAT 2140 , MAT 2240 , MAT 2250 , STA 120, or STA 1200 ; or C- or better in CHM 121 and CHM 121L.

courses.title: General Chemistry Laboratory I
courses.description: [GE 5C] Laboratory experiments to illustrate and enhance lecture topics in CHM 1210 . Basic laboratory techniques and practices. Product fee required. Corequisite(s): CHM 1210 .
courses.prerequisites: SAT Math>=550; ACT Math>=23; ALEKS >=76; C or better in MAT 12, 105, 106, 112, 114, 115, 116, 120, 125, 130, 191, 214, 216, 224, MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , MAT 1060 , MAT 1070 , MAT 1140 , MAT 1150 , MAT 1200 , MAT 1250 , MAT 1300 , MAT 1310 , MAT 1910 , MAT 2140 , MAT 2240 , MAT 2250 , STA 120, or STA 1200 ; or C- or better in CHM 121 and CHM 121L.

courses.title: Introduction to Soil Science
courses.description: A comprehensive overview of the fundamental concepts and principles of soil science, emphasizing the critical role soils play in ecosystems, agriculture, and environmental sustainability. Explore the formation, classification, and properties of soils, including physical, chemical, and biological aspects. Topics will cover soil ecology, nutrient management, soil conservation practices, and the impact of human activities on soil health. Corequisite(s): PLT 2310L .

courses.title: Introduction to Soil Science Laboratory
courses.description: Essential techniques for analyzing soil properties, including texture, structure, pH, moisture content, and nutrient composition. Through guided laboratory exercises, they will develop skills in soil sampling, testing methods, and data interpretation, fostering a deeper understanding of soil and management practices. Corequisite(s): PLT 2310 .

courses.title: Soil Fertility and Fertilizers
courses.description: Examine soil nutrient availability, the impact of fertilizers on plant mineral nutrition and crop production, and the interpretation of soil test results for fertilization decisions. Addresses the economic and environmental implications of fertilizer use, emphasizing sustainable practices and the role of precision agriculture in enhancing nutrient use efficiency. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement. Corequisite(s): PLT 3320LW .
courses.prerequisites: PLT 2310 , PLT 2310L , and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Soil Chemistry
courses.description: Examines the fundamental chemical principles governing reactions in soils, with emphasis on soil mineralogy, surface chemistry, soil carbon transformations, and redox processes. Topics will focus on the theoretical basis of modern analytical and spectroscopic techniques used to study soil chemical processes.

courses.title: Soil Physics
courses.description: Methods to characterize physical attributes of soil. Soil particle size distribution and structure, nature and behavior of clay, state and movement of water and solutes in saturated and unsaturated soil conditions, gas and energy exchange between soil and atmosphere, principles of rheology. Corequisite(s): GSC 4320L .
courses.prerequisites: GSC 141L, GSC 1410L , PLT 231 or PLT 2310 ; and Upper Division or Graduate Standing.

courses.title: Soil Physics Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory and field investigations of Soil Physics. Laboratories emphasize physical attributes of soil. Soil particle size distribution and structure, nature and behavior of clay, state and movement of water and solutes in saturated and unsaturated soil conditions, gas and energy exchange between soil and atmosphere, principles of rheology. Corequisite(s): GSC 4320 .
courses.prerequisites: GSC 141L, GSC 1410L , PLT 231 or PLT 2310 ; and Upper Division or Graduate standing.

courses.title: Sprinkler/Drip Irrigation
courses.description: An introduction to sprinkler and drip micro-irrigation systems and techniques. Systems will be discussed that apply to landscape and agronomic crops. Water savings and management will be a major part of this course.

courses.title: Environmental Toxicology
courses.description: Survey and analyses of the effects of civilization on the environment. Emphasis will be placed on the effects of agriculture and other forms of commerce on food, water, air, soil, and human health.
courses.prerequisites: PLT 231 or PLT 2310 ; and PLT 231L or PLT 2310L .

courses.title: Ecotoxicology
courses.description: How to think critically about pollutants in the environment - how they interact with biological systems, and how they affect individuals, populations, communities, ecosystems, and our society. Promoting an understanding of: the scientific process for investigating the effects of toxicants on biological systems; the major types and sources of contamination, including environmental disasters; how biological systems and society are affected by, and respond to the issues that pollutants create.

courses.title: Geospatial Analysis of Soils, Plants, and People
courses.description: Exploration of mapping, GIS, and remote sensing can be applied to real-world problems in agriculture and the environment. Includes hands-on techniques for collecting, analyzing, and visualizing spatial data, with applications ranging from soils and nutrients to crops and ecosystems. Taught in three sections by faculty with expertise in soil science, ethnobotany, and precision agriculture, the course highlights how mapping tools support soil sampling, nutrient management, irrigation, adaptive farming, and environmental decision-making. Includes the implementation of practical skills in GIS, drone imaging, and remote sensing, preparing them to address challenges in sustainable agriculture and natural resource management.

courses.title: Special Topics for Upper Division Students
courses.description: Group study at an advanced level of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
